Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace README and rollout evidence, then I’ll consult the required fish-control bookshelf before proposing or editing the policy. I’ll keep the implementation to exactly one candidate and verify both required documentation updates.

The README confirms that policy edits must wait until the candidate-specific visual diagnosis and hypothesis are written. I’m also using the “read wake visual signals first” skill because this task requires interpreting the paired 3D rollout views before changing control logic.

The inherited guidance points to a specific unresolved mechanism: a geometry-persistent, opposite-sign posterior S-bend for the powered lower near-miss. I’ll test that interpretation against the actual sampled rollouts and bookshelf invariants before committing to it.

All four visual sheets show the same high-level failure topology: a coherent, self-propelled reverse-vortex street; approach to roughly 2.4–2.5L around 19T; then a near-vertical departure and left-domain exit around 31T. The variants alter the near miss only slightly, so I’m now checking whether their gates actually persisted during the missed turn and whether force/action limits rule out adding authority.

The cross-check confirms the best sampled selector is the yaw-gated brake (`2.385L` minimum), but all four candidates retain the same powered lower exit. A sampled optimizer branch also quantifies near-perfect beat-lock between yaw rate and anterior joint velocity, so the next candidate will treat yaw only as a half-cycle selector and change the actuator action: smoothly reverse the authority that the brake discarded, without increasing far-field wave amplitude. This is the bookshelf’s asymmetric-flapping/phase-modulation invariant, translated into body-frame target geometry and measured joint/yaw state.

The inherited logs sharpen the distinction: a response-gated equilibrium residual later reached only about `2.444L`, so the new action must not be another mean-tail bias. I’m recording the pre-edit diagnosis now, then I’ll implement one smooth polarity reallocation of the posterior traveling-wave component under the already evidenced selector.

The one candidate is now implemented as a response-selected counterstroke: outside the terminal gate it is algebraically the sampled carrier; at full gating the posterior wave multiplier reaches `-0.30`, so no wave magnitude exceeds cruise authority. I’m invoking the required non-CFD check runner now, including semantic guidance, policy contract/schema, and solver-boundary checks.

Two of the three required checks passed. The guidance check found a pre-existing duplicate “copied to guidance” parent marker in the rendered README—the same issue documented in inherited logs—so I’m removing only that duplicate marker and rerunning the check.

The repaired check now passes, so the full mandated check runner is green. I’m doing a final evidence-local validation next: parameter ownership, reflection symmetry, gate locality, multiplier bounds, and the repository’s non-CFD tests. No CFD rollout will be run.

All 324 non-CFD tests pass. The direct probes also confirm 21/21 referenced parameters are owned, exact reflection equivariance, finite clamped extreme-state output, negligible far-field activation (`0.00065`), near-complete corrective-half-cycle release, and the intended near wrong-way counterstroke (`-0.182` multiplier at a representative `2.4L` state). I’m recording those as implementation checks—not CFD evidence—then doing the final checker rerun.

The final guidance check passes after the implementation notes were added. The candidate is complete: one policy file, one candidate-specific evidence log, and one material reusable guidance lesson; formal CFD remains intentionally deferred to EvE.

Implemented exactly one candidate: a response-selected posterior counterstroke that reallocates discarded braking authority without increasing cruise-wave magnitude.

- [Evidence and bookshelf notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [Reusable control lesson](guidance/control_experience.md:88)

Validation passed: all check-runner checks, parameter ownership, symmetry/bounds/locality probes, and 324 non-CFD tests. Formal CFD was not run, as required.
